input.command:
python3 << 'EOF'
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
a = np.asarray(im).astype(float)
print("shape", a.shape)
# check if grayscale (R==G==B everywhere)
diff = np.abs(a[...,0]-a[...,1]).max(), np.abs(a[...,1]-a[...,2]).max(), np.abs(a[...,0]-a[...,2]).max()
print("max channel diffs:", diff)
lum = a.mean(axis=2)  # H x W
colmean = lum.mean(axis=0)  # per column
print("col mean stats: min %.1f max %.1f overall %.1f" % (colmean.min(), colmean.max(), colmean.mean()))
# Detect stripe width: how many distinct values along a row? columns should be uniform if each stripe is constant
colstd = lum.std(axis=0)
print("columns with vertical variation (std>1):", (colstd>1).sum(), "of", lum.shape[1])
# find steps: positions where colmean jumps
d = np.diff(colmean)
edges = np.where(np.abs(d)>3)[0]
print("num big edges:", len(edges))
print("first 50 edges:", edges[:50])
print("edge gaps:", np.unique(np.diff(edges), return_counts=True) if len(edges)>1 else None)
EOF

python3 << 'EOF'
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
a = np.asarray(im).astype(float).mean(axis=2)  # 200x1000
p = a.mean(axis=0)  # 1000 luminance profile
# summarize in 40 bins of 25 columns
bins = p.reshape(40,25).mean(axis=1)
for i,b in enumerate(bins):
    bar = '#'*int(b/3)
    print(f"{i*25:4d}-{i*25+24:4d} mean={b:6.1f} {bar}")
print()
# brightest columns
idx = np.argsort(p)[::-1][:20]
print("brightest cols (col,lum):", [(int(i), round(p[i],1)) for i in sorted(idx)])
idx = np.argsort(p)[:20]
print("darkest cols  (col,lum):", [(int(i), round(p[i],1)) for i in sorted(idx)])
# fraction of columns > 100 (bright), < 20 (black)
print("frac>100:", (p>100).mean(), "frac>120:", (p>120).mean(), "frac<20:", (p<20).mean(), "frac<40:", (p<40).mean(), "frac 40-90:", ((p>=40)&(p<=90)).mean())
# histogram
hist,edges = np.histogram(p, bins=16, range=(0,160))
print("hist:", hist.tolist())
print("bin edges:", edges.tolist())
EOF

# Movie Barcode Generator
![github-bighero6](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1192790/11238640/1f7ea5ac-8e3b-11e5-8c2b-e00758b1ec19.png)

Turn video files into 'barcodes' where vertical lines represent the average colour of individual frames. [Example album.](http://imgur.com/gallery/Pw6LD/) Uses code [published by zulko](http://zulko.github.io/blog/2013/09/27/read-and-write-video-frames-in-python-using-ffmpeg/).

**Requirements:**
* [ffmpeg](https://www.ffmpeg.org/)
* Python and [Python Imaging Library](http://www.pythonware.com/products/pil/)
 
**Usage:**  
    *python process_video.py inputfile width height*  
e.g.  
    *python process_video.py bigbuckbunny.mp4 320 180*

**Tips:**
* If it doesn't work on Windows, you might have to change FFMPEG_BIN from "ffmpeg" to "ffmpeg.exe"
* Use low resolution videos! They provide identical results but are processed exponentially faster than high definition videos (I've seen above 1300fps). You're smearing all the details anyway.
* By default, the resulting image will be as wide as the number of frames in the movie - probably several tens of thousands of pixels. However due to the nature of PNG files, it will only be a few hundred kilobytes! But you will need to use Photoshop or similar to format the images to your liking... or patch my code so the user can specify output size!
 
**Details:**

You may have seen sites like [moviebarcode](http://moviebarcode.tumblr.com/), [The Colors of Motion](http://thecolorsofmotion.com/) or the [Movie Barcode Generator](http://arcanesanctum.net/movie-barcode-generator/). In short, they compress a movie into a single image, with vertical lines representing the average colours of sequential frames. Ideally this gives a glanceable idea of the movie's colour palette.

While moviebarcode squashes each frame to a single pixel width (preserving some vertical gradients), this script uses a similar process to The Colors of Motion (a single colour per frame). First find the average RGB values of all pixels in a single frame:

![github-process-1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1192790/11238530/715e0d1e-8e3a-11e5-9736-68f2e67d21fc.png)

And then to repeat the process for all frames:

![github-process-2](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1192790/11238535/7664e6ac-8e3a-11e5-8989-6be607fa395e.png)

This should work with any movie file ffmpeg can handle (though in practice I've only tested it with mp4 files). 

**Quibbles:**
* I'd love to autodetect the video resolution but this seems to require grepping some ffmpeg output.
* There ~~may be~~ is almost certainly a faster approach than the one I'm using. Perhaps I should only take every nth frame?
* Users should be able to specify an output size instead of having to manually edit the file.

(Video stills: [Big Buck Bunny](https://peach.blender.org/download/))

import re
data = open('/tmp/imgur.html', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()

***The Kid*** is a 1921 American [silent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_film "Silent film") [comedy-drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_drama "Comedy drama") written, produced, directed by and starring [Charlie Chaplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Chaplin "Charlie Chaplin"), and features [Jackie Coogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Coogan "Jackie Coogan")[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) as his foundling baby, adopted son and sidekick. This was Chaplin's first feature-length film as a director. It was a huge success and was the second-highest-grossing film in 1921\.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) Now considered one of the [greatest films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_films_voted_the_best "List of films voted the best") of the silent era,[\[6\]](#cite_note-:1-6) it was selected for preservation in the United States [National Film Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Registry "National Film Registry") by the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress") in 2011\.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Kid_\(1921_film\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

With much anguish, an unwed mother abandons her child, placing him in an expensive automobile with a handwritten note: "Please love and care for this orphan child". Two thieves steal the car and leave the baby in an alley, where he is found by [The Tramp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tramp "The Tramp"). After some attempts to hand off the child to various passers-by, he finds the note and his heart melts. He takes the boy home, names him John and adjusts his household furniture for him. Meanwhile, the Mother has a change of heart and returns for her baby; when she learns that the car has been stolen, she faints.

Five years pass. The Kid and the Tramp live in the same tiny room; they have little money but much love. They support themselves in a minor scheme: the Kid throws stones to break windows so that the Tramp, working as a [glazier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glazier "Glazier"), can be paid to repair them. Meanwhile, the Mother has become a wealthy actress and does charity by giving presents to poor children. By chance, as she does so, the Mother and the Kid unknowingly cross paths.

The Kid later gets into a fight with another local boy as people in the area gather to watch the spectacle. The Kid wins, drawing the ire of the other boy's older brother, who attacks the Tramp as a result. The Mother breaks up the fight, but it starts again after she leaves and the Tramp keeps beating the "Big Brother" over the head with a brick between swings until he totters away.

Shortly afterward, the Mother advises the Tramp to call a doctor after the Kid falls ill. The doctor discovers that the Tramp is not the Kid's father and notifies authorities. Two men come to take the boy to an orphanage, but after a fight and a chase, the Tramp and the boy remain side by side. When the Mother comes back to see how the boy is doing she encounters the doctor, who shows her the note (which he had taken from the Tramp); she recognizes it as the one she left with her baby years ago.

Now fugitives, the Tramp and the boy spend the night in a [flophouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flophouse "Flophouse"). Its proprietor learns of a $1,000 reward offered by the authorities and takes the Kid to the police station, while the Tramp is asleep. As the tearful Mother is reunited with her long-lost child, the Tramp searches frantically for the missing boy. Unsuccessful, he returns to the doorway of their humble lodgings, where he falls asleep, entering a "Dreamland" where his neighbors have turned into angels and devils. A policeman awakes him and drives him off to a mansion. There the door is opened by the Mother and the Kid, who jumps into the Tramp's arms, and he is welcomed in.

## Production

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Kid_\(1921_film\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")\]

Chaplin wrote, produced, directed, edited and starred in *The Kid*, and later composed a score. Innovative in its combination of comedic and dramatic elements,[\[11\]](#cite_note-:2-11) the film is considered one of the greatest of the silent era.[\[6\]](#cite_note-:1-6) Chaplin biographer Jeffrey Vance maintains that, with its "perfect blend of comedy and drama, \[it\] is arguably Chaplin's most personal and autobiographical work.”[\[12\]](#cite_note-loc.gov-12)

The film made Coogan, then a [vaudeville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaudeville "Vaudeville") performer, into the first major child star of the movies. Author Dan Kamin speculates that the depth of the relationship portrayed in the film may have been connected with the death of Chaplin's firstborn infant son just ten days before the production began.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Jackie_Coogan%2C_The_Kid_%281921%29.jpg/330px-Jackie_Coogan%2C_The_Kid_%281921%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jackie_Coogan,_The_Kid_\(1921\).jpg)

"The Kid" pleading to be left with his "father", Chaplin

First National wanted to release the film as three two-reel comedies, not a seven-reel feature.[\[14\]](#cite_note-:0-14) Chaplin wanted the film released as a complete work. Releasing it as three separate short films also meant First National owed Chaplin a much smaller salary.[\[14\]](#cite_note-:0-14) After production was completed in 1920, the film was caught up in the divorce actions of Chaplin's first wife [Mildred Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mildred_Harris "Mildred Harris"), who sought to attach Chaplin's assets. Chaplin and his associates smuggled the raw negative to [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City") and edited it in a room at the [Hotel Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel_Utah_\(Salt_Lake_City\) "Hotel Utah (Salt Lake City)").[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) To release the complete film and avoid it being part of his divorce proceedings, Chaplin showed First National executives a cut of the film. He used this screening to re-negotiate his contract.[\[14\]](#cite_note-:0-14) Before releasing the film, Chaplin negotiated to receive an enhanced financial deal based on the success of the final film. This included 50% of the box-office once First National's budget of $1.5 million had been reached and full ownership returned to Chaplin after five years.[\[14\]](#cite_note-:0-14)

Chaplin eventually removed scenes he believed too sentimental for modern audiences and composed and recorded a new musical score for the film's theatrical reissue. This re-edited version of *The Kid* had its world premiere as the Film Society of Lincoln Center gala tribute to Chaplin held on April 4, 1972, at Philharmonic Hall, New York City, with Chaplin in attendance.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Kid_\(1921_film\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reception")\]

*The Kid* premiered on January 21, 1921, at Carnegie Hall in New York City as a benefit for the Children's Fund of the National Board of Review of Motion Pictures.[\[12\]](#cite_note-loc.gov-12)

*The Kid* was acclaimed by film critics upon its release.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) The February 5, 1921 issue of *Exhibitor's Herald*, contained a full-spread advertisement for the film playing at the Randolph Theatre. The advertisement from First National Pictures featured high praise from Chicago-based newspapers including this review from *The Chicago Herald and Examiner*:

> *The Kid* settles once and for all the question as to who is the greatest theatrical artist in the world. Chaplin does some of the finest, most delicately shaded acting you ever saw anywhere, and for every slapstick furore in it there is a classic, exquisite scene. His action are riotous, convulsive, irresistible. The gentlest grandmother will bust a midriff. He's the best Hamlet alive today. Jackie Coogan is the best child actor you ever saw. Women wept just to see him. *The Kid* is two fisted. It's right glove is packed with the pearls of tears, its left with the horseshoe of laughter. The picture is perfection. Six reels that seem like one; six reels that are funnier than the work of any other human being; six reels that are sadder and simpler than anything in pictures; six reels that will atone for anything the movies have ever done.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

A reviewer from *Theatre Magazine* glowingly wrote: "\[Chaplin's\] new picture, *The Kid*, certainly outdoes in humor and the special brand of Chaplin pathos anything this popular film star has yet produced. There are almost as many tears as laughs in the new First National release--which proves the contention that Chaplin is almost as good a tragedian as he is a comedian. *The Kid* may be counted as a screen masterpiece."

The reviewer for *The New York Times* gave more of a mixed reception to the film, writing: "Charlie Chaplin is himself again \- at his best, in some ways better than his previous best, and also, it is to be regretted, at his worst, only not with so much of his worst as has spoiled some of his earlier pictures." The reviewer praises the plot, the comedy, the characters, and the "balance of sadness" with Chaplin being "more of a comedian than a clown", but lamented elements of "vulgarity, or coarseness".[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

## Legacy

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Kid_\(1921_film\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Legacy")\]

Chaplin biographer [Jeffrey Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Vance "Jeffrey Vance") writes of the legacy of Chaplin's *The Kid*: "*The Kid* remains an important contribution to the art of film, not only because of Chaplin's innovative use of dramatic sequences within a feature-length comedy, but also because of the revelations *The Kid* provides about its creator. Undoubtedly, when Chaplin penned the preface to *The Kid*, "A picture with a smile—and perhaps, a tear", he had his own artistic credo—and life—in mind."[\[11\]](#cite_note-:2-11) [Mary Pickford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Pickford "Mary Pickford") said of the film, "*The Kid* is one of the finest examples of the screen language, depending upon its actions rather than upon subtitles".[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)

*The Kid*

In December 2011, *The Kid* was chosen to be preserved in the Library of Congress' National Film Registry.[\[21\]](#cite_note-LOC-21) The registry stated that the film is "an artful melding of touching drama, social commentary and inventive comedy" and praised Chaplin's ability to "sustain his artistry beyond the length of his usual short subjects and could deftly elicit a variety of emotions from his audiences by skillfully blending slapstick and pathos."[\[21\]](#cite_note-LOC-21)

In 2016, the [Dallas Chamber Symphony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Chamber_Symphony "Dallas Chamber Symphony") commissioned an original film score for *The Kid* from composer [Craig Safan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Safan "Craig Safan").[\[22\]](#cite_note-22)[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) The score premiered during a concert screening on February 21, 2017, at [Moody Performance Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moody_Performance_Hall "Moody Performance Hall") with [Richard McKay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_McKay "Richard McKay") conducting.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)

In May 2017, it was announced that an animated science-fiction adaptation of *The Kid* was in the works at French animation studio [Superprod Animation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superprod_Group "Superprod Group"), with [Big Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Beach_\(company\) "Big Beach (company)") and Luxembourg-based production company Bidibul Productions producing, and [FilmNation Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FilmNation_Entertainment "FilmNation Entertainment") to distribute it internationally.[\[25\]](#cite_note-25)

As of January 2021, *The Kid* has earned a [100% rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_films_with_a_100%25_rating_on_Rotten_Tomatoes "List of films with a 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes") on Rotten Tomatoes, based on 50 reviews, with a weighted average of 8\.6/10. The website's critical consensus says: "Charles Chaplin's irascible Tramp is given able support from Jackie Coogan as The Kid in this slapstick masterpiece, balancing the guffaws with moments of disarming poignancy".[\[26\]](#cite_note-26)

*The Kid* was one of many silent films to film in a one-block alley near [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Boulevard "Hollywood Boulevard") and [Cahuenga Boulevard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cahuenga_Boulevard "Cahuenga Boulevard"). The alley was later renamed [Chaplin-Keaton-Lloyd Alley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaplin-Keaton-Lloyd_Alley "Chaplin-Keaton-Lloyd Alley") in recognition of this and other films.[\[27\]](#cite_note-27)

***The Kid*** is a 1921 American [silent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_film "Silent film") [comedy-drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_drama "Comedy drama") written, produced, directed by and starring [Charlie Chaplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Chaplin "Charlie Chaplin"), and features [Jackie Coogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Coogan "Jackie Coogan")[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) as his foundling baby, adopted son and sidekick. This was Chaplin's first feature-length film as a director. It was a huge success and was the second-highest-grossing film in 1921\.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) Now considered one of the [greatest films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_films_voted_the_best "List of films voted the best") of the silent era,[\[6\]](#cite_note-:1-6) it was selected for preservation in the United States [National Film Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Registry "National Film Registry") by the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress") in 2011\.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Kid_\(1921_film\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

With much anguish, an unwed mother abandons her child, placing him in an expensive automobile with a handwritten note: "Please love and care for this orphan child". Two thieves steal the car and leave the baby in an alley, where he is found by [The Tramp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tramp "The Tramp"). After some attempts to hand off the child to various passers-by, he finds the note and his heart melts. He takes the boy home, names him John and adjusts his household furniture for him. Meanwhile, the Mother has a change of heart and returns for her baby; when she learns that the car has been stolen, she faints.

Five years pass. The Kid and the Tramp live in the same tiny room; they have little money but much love. They support themselves in a minor scheme: the Kid throws stones to break windows so that the Tramp, working as a [glazier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glazier "Glazier"), can be paid to repair them. Meanwhile, the Mother has become a wealthy actress and does charity by giving presents to poor children. By chance, as she does so, the Mother and the Kid unknowingly cross paths.

The Kid later gets into a fight with another local boy as people in the area gather to watch the spectacle. The Kid wins, drawing the ire of the other boy's older brother, who attacks the Tramp as a result. The Mother breaks up the fight, but it starts again after she leaves and the Tramp keeps beating the "Big Brother" over the head with a brick between swings until he totters away.

Shortly afterward, the Mother advises the Tramp to call a doctor after the Kid falls ill. The doctor discovers that the Tramp is not the Kid's father and notifies authorities. Two men come to take the boy to an orphanage, but after a fight and a chase, the Tramp and the boy remain side by side. When the Mother comes back to see how the boy is doing she encounters the doctor, who shows her the note (which he had taken from the Tramp); she recognizes it as the one she left with her baby years ago.

Now fugitives, the Tramp and the boy spend the night in a [flophouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flophouse "Flophouse"). Its proprietor learns of a $1,000 reward offered by the authorities and takes the Kid to the police station, while the Tramp is asleep. As the tearful Mother is reunited with her long-lost child, the Tramp searches frantically for the missing boy. Unsuccessful, he returns to the doorway of their humble lodgings, where he falls asleep, entering a "Dreamland" where his neighbors have turned into angels and devils. A policeman awakes him and drives him off to a mansion. There the door is opened by the Mother and the Kid, who jumps into the Tramp's arms, and he is welcomed in.

## Production

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Kid_\(1921_film\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")\]

Chaplin wrote, produced, directed, edited and starred in *The Kid*, and later composed a score. Innovative in its combination of comedic and dramatic elements,[\[11\]](#cite_note-:2-11) the film is considered one of the greatest of the silent era.[\[6\]](#cite_note-:1-6) Chaplin biographer Jeffrey Vance maintains that, with its "perfect blend of comedy and drama, \[it\] is arguably Chaplin's most personal and autobiographical work.”[\[12\]](#cite_note-loc.gov-12)

The film made Coogan, then a [vaudeville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaudeville "Vaudeville") performer, into the first major child star of the movies. Author Dan Kamin speculates that the depth of the relationship portrayed in the film may have been connected with the death of Chaplin's firstborn infant son just ten days before the production began.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Jackie_Coogan%2C_The_Kid_%281921%29.jpg/330px-Jackie_Coogan%2C_The_Kid_%281921%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jackie_Coogan,_The_Kid_\(1921\).jpg)

"The Kid" pleading to be left with his "father", Chaplin

First National wanted to release the film as three two-reel comedies, not a seven-reel feature.[\[14\]](#cite_note-:0-14) Chaplin wanted the film released as a complete work. Releasing it as three separate short films also meant First National owed Chaplin a much smaller salary.[\[14\]](#cite_note-:0-14) After production was completed in 1920, the film was caught up in the divorce actions of Chaplin's first wife [Mildred Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mildred_Harris "Mildred Harris"), who sought to attach Chaplin's assets. Chaplin and his associates smuggled the raw negative to [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City") and edited it in a room at the [Hotel Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel_Utah_\(Salt_Lake_City\) "Hotel Utah (Salt Lake City)").[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) To release the complete film and avoid it being part of his divorce proceedings, Chaplin showed First National executives a cut of the film. He used this screening to re-negotiate his contract.[\[14\]](#cite_note-:0-14) Before releasing the film, Chaplin negotiated to receive an enhanced financial deal based on the success of the final film. This included 50% of the box-office once First National's budget of $1.5 million had been reached and full ownership returned to Chaplin after five years.[\[14\]](#cite_note-:0-14)

Chaplin eventually removed scenes he believed too sentimental for modern audiences and composed and recorded a new musical score for the film's theatrical reissue. This re-edited version of *The Kid* had its world premiere as the Film Society of Lincoln Center gala tribute to Chaplin held on April 4, 1972, at Philharmonic Hall, New York City, with Chaplin in attendance.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Kid_\(1921_film\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reception")\]

*The Kid* premiered on January 21, 1921, at Carnegie Hall in New York City as a benefit for the Children's Fund of the National Board of Review of Motion Pictures.[\[12\]](#cite_note-loc.gov-12)

*The Kid* was acclaimed by film critics upon its release.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) The February 5, 1921 issue of *Exhibitor's Herald*, contained a full-spread advertisement for the film playing at the Randolph Theatre. The advertisement from First National Pictures featured high praise from Chicago-based newspapers including this review from *The Chicago Herald and Examiner*:

> *The Kid* settles once and for all the question as to who is the greatest theatrical artist in the world. Chaplin does some of the finest, most delicately shaded acting you ever saw anywhere, and for every slapstick furore in it there is a classic, exquisite scene. His action are riotous, convulsive, irresistible. The gentlest grandmother will bust a midriff. He's the best Hamlet alive today. Jackie Coogan is the best child actor you ever saw. Women wept just to see him. *The Kid* is two fisted. It's right glove is packed with the pearls of tears, its left with the horseshoe of laughter. The picture is perfection. Six reels that seem like one; six reels that are funnier than the work of any other human being; six reels that are sadder and simpler than anything in pictures; six reels that will atone for anything the movies have ever done.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

A reviewer from *Theatre Magazine* glowingly wrote: "\[Chaplin's\] new picture, *The Kid*, certainly outdoes in humor and the special brand of Chaplin pathos anything this popular film star has yet produced. There are almost as many tears as laughs in the new First National release--which proves the contention that Chaplin is almost as good a tragedian as he is a comedian. *The Kid* may be counted as a screen masterpiece."

The reviewer for *The New York Times* gave more of a mixed reception to the film, writing: "Charlie Chaplin is himself again \- at his best, in some ways better than his previous best, and also, it is to be regretted, at his worst, only not with so much of his worst as has spoiled some of his earlier pictures." The reviewer praises the plot, the comedy, the characters, and the "balance of sadness" with Chaplin being "more of a comedian than a clown", but lamented elements of "vulgarity, or coarseness".[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

## Legacy

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Kid_\(1921_film\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Legacy")\]

Chaplin biographer [Jeffrey Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Vance "Jeffrey Vance") writes of the legacy of Chaplin's *The Kid*: "*The Kid* remains an important contribution to the art of film, not only because of Chaplin's innovative use of dramatic sequences within a feature-length comedy, but also because of the revelations *The Kid* provides about its creator. Undoubtedly, when Chaplin penned the preface to *The Kid*, "A picture with a smile—and perhaps, a tear", he had his own artistic credo—and life—in mind."[\[11\]](#cite_note-:2-11) [Mary Pickford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Pickford "Mary Pickford") said of the film, "*The Kid* is one of the finest examples of the screen language, depending upon its actions rather than upon subtitles".[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)

*The Kid*

In December 2011, *The Kid* was chosen to be preserved in the Library of Congress' National Film Registry.[\[21\]](#cite_note-LOC-21) The registry stated that the film is "an artful melding of touching drama, social commentary and inventive comedy" and praised Chaplin's ability to "sustain his artistry beyond the length of his usual short subjects and could deftly elicit a variety of emotions from his audiences by skillfully blending slapstick and pathos."[\[21\]](#cite_note-LOC-21)

In 2016, the [Dallas Chamber Symphony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Chamber_Symphony "Dallas Chamber Symphony") commissioned an original film score for *The Kid* from composer [Craig Safan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Safan "Craig Safan").[\[22\]](#cite_note-22)[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) The score premiered during a concert screening on February 21, 2017, at [Moody Performance Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moody_Performance_Hall "Moody Performance Hall") with [Richard McKay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_McKay "Richard McKay") conducting.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)

In May 2017, it was announced that an animated science-fiction adaptation of *The Kid* was in the works at French animation studio [Superprod Animation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superprod_Group "Superprod Group"), with [Big Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Beach_\(company\) "Big Beach (company)") and Luxembourg-based production company Bidibul Productions producing, and [FilmNation Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FilmNation_Entertainment "FilmNation Entertainment") to distribute it internationally.[\[25\]](#cite_note-25)

As of January 2021, *The Kid* has earned a [100% rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_films_with_a_100%25_rating_on_Rotten_Tomatoes "List of films with a 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes") on Rotten Tomatoes, based on 50 reviews, with a weighted average of 8\.6/10. The website's critical consensus says: "Charles Chaplin's irascible Tramp is given able support from Jackie Coogan as The Kid in this slapstick masterpiece, balancing the guffaws with moments of disarming poignancy".[\[26\]](#cite_note-26)

*The Kid* was one of many silent films to film in a one-block alley near [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Boulevard "Hollywood Boulevard") and [Cahuenga Boulevard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cahuenga_Boulevard "Cahuenga Boulevard"). The alley was later renamed [Chaplin-Keaton-Lloyd Alley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaplin-Keaton-Lloyd_Alley "Chaplin-Keaton-Lloyd Alley") in recognition of this and other films.[\[27\]](#cite_note-27)

from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
a = np.asarray(im).astype(float)  # H,W,3
# per-column mean RGB
col = a.mean(axis=0)  # W,3
r,g,b = col[:,0], col[:,1], col[:,2]
rb = r-b; gr = g-r; gb = g-b
print("R-B stats: min %.2f max %.2f" % (rb.min(), rb.max()))
print("G-R stats: min %.2f max %.2f" % (gr.min(), gr.max()))
# find columns with |R-B| >= 2
idx = np.where(np.abs(rb)>=2)[0]
print("cols |R-B|>=2:", idx.tolist()[:80], "..." if len(idx)>80 else "", "count:", len(idx))
# summarize R-B in 50 bins
bins = rb.reshape(50,20).mean(axis=1)
for i,v in enumerate(bins):
    tag=''
    if v>0.5: tag='WARM/RED'
    if v<-0.5: tag='COOL/BLUE'
    print(f"{i*2:3d}-{i*2+2:3d}% R-B={v:+.2f} {tag}")
EOF

for key, ident in ITEMS.items():

    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(12) as ex:

python3 << 'EOF'
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np, glob, re, json

def profile(ident_prefix):
    files = sorted(glob.glob(f'/tmp/thumbs/{ident_prefix}_*.jpg'))
    ts, lum = [], []
    for f in files:
        t = int(re.search(r'_(\d+)\.jpg', f).group(1))
        im = Image.open(f).convert('RGB')
        a = np.asarray(im).astype(float)
        ts.append(t); lum.append(a.mean())
    ts = np.array(ts, float); lum = np.array(lum)
    return ts, lum

mine = np.load('/tmp/profile.npy')  # 1000 stripes

def smooth(y, k=3):
    ker = np.ones(2*k+1)/(2*k+1)
    return np.convolve(np.pad(y, k, mode='edge'), ker, mode='valid')

def compare(ident_prefix, runtime, k=3):
    ts, lum = profile(ident_prefix)
    T = ts.max()  # actual span
    x = ts/T  # relative 0..1
    xs = np.linspace(0, len(mine)-1, 1000)
    xi = (x*(999)).round().clip(0,999).astype(int)
    ref = mine[xi]
    a = smooth(lum, k); b = smooth(ref, k)

from PIL import Image
import numpy as np, glob, re, json
from scipy import stats if False else None  # no scipy; implement spearman manually

ITEMS = {
 'general':  ['the-general-keaton-and-bruckman-1926-high-quality-1080p-t-o-p-swu-fc',
              'TheGeneral1926BusterKeatonProductionUsa','TheGeneral_201312','buster-keaton-the-general-1927'],
 'kid':      ['the-kid_202509','Brzdac1921'],
 'metropolis':['metropolis-1927_202511','metropolis_202511','metropolis-1927-english-titles','metropolis-1927-4-k-u-rnemls-bwry'],
 'potemkin': ['BattleshipPotemkin1925','battleship-potemkin-1925_202607','o-encouracado-potemkin',
              'PhantasmagoriaTheater-BattleshipPotemkin1925396'],
 '39steps':  ['the-39-steps-1935','the-39-steps-39-basamak-alfred-hitchcock-turkce-dublaj','the-39-steps-1935_202609'],
 'allquiet': ['all-quiet-on-the-western-front_202601','all-quiet-on-the-western-front-1930_202604'],
 'joan':     ['passion-joan-of-arc','the-passion-of-joan-of-arc-1928-by-carl-theodor-dreyer',
              'passion-of-joan-of-arc-the-carl-theodor-dreyer-1928',
              'rocking-silents-presents-the-passion-of-joan-of-arc-music-by-mazzy-sta','the-passion-of-joan-of-arc'],
}

def thumb_lum(f):
    a = np.asarray(Image.open(f).convert('RGB')).astype(float).mean(axis=2)
    rows = a.mean(axis=1); cols = a.mean(axis=0)
    rr = np.where(rows>12)[0]; cc = np.where(cols>12)[0]
    if len(rr)==0 or len(cc)==0:
        return a.mean()
    return a[rr[0]:rr[-1]+1, cc[0]:cc[-1]+1].mean()

def item_profile(ident):
    files = sorted(glob.glob(f'/tmp/thumbs/{ident}__*.jpg')) or sorted(glob.glob(f'/tmp/thumbs/{ident}_*.jpg'))
    # avoid mixing the two patterns for the same ident
    if glob.glob(f'/tmp/thumbs/{ident}__*.jpg'):
        files = sorted(glob.glob(f'/tmp/thumbs/{ident}__*.jpg'))
    else:
        files = sorted(glob.glob(f'/tmp/thumbs/{ident}_*.jpg'))
    ts, lum = [], []
    for f in files:
        m = re.search(r'__(\d+)\.jpg$', f) or re.search(r'_(\d+)\.jpg$', f)
        ts.append(int(m.group(1)))
        lum.append(thumb_lum(f))
    ts = np.array(ts, float); lum = np.array(lum)
    # drop duplicate times
    order = np.argsort(ts)
    ts, lum = ts[order], lum[order]
    keep = np.ones(len(ts), bool)
    keep[1:] = ts[1:] != ts[:-1]
    return ts[keep], lum[keep]

mine = np.load('/tmp/profile.npy')

def smooth(y,k):
    ker=np.ones(2*k+1)/(2*k+1)
    return np.convolve(np.pad(y,k,mode='edge'),ker,mode='valid')

def ranknorm(y):
    r = np.argsort(np.argsort(y))
    return r/(len(y)-1)

def spearman(a,b):
    ra, rb = ranknorm(a), ranknorm(b)
    ra = ra - ra.mean(); rb = rb - rb.mean()
    return float((ra*rb).sum()/np.sqrt((ra*ra).sum()*(rb*rb).sum()))

def pearson(a,b):
    a=a-a.mean(); b=b-b.mean()
    return float((a*b).sum()/np.sqrt((a*a).sum()*(b*b).sum()))

def item_corr(ident, k, method='spearman', shift_scan=0):
    ts, lum = item_profile(ident)
    T = ts.max()
    x = ts/T
    xi = (x*999).round().clip(0,999).astype(int)
    ref = mine[xi]
    if shift_scan:
        best=-1
        for sh in range(-shift_scan, shift_scan+1):
            xs = np.clip(xi+sh, 0, 999)
            r_ = mine[xs]
            a_ = smooth(lum,k); b_ = smooth(r_,k)
            c = spearman(a_,b_) if method=='spearman' else pearson(a_,b_)
            if c>best: best=c
        return best, len(ts), T
    a = smooth(lum,k); b = smooth(ref,k)
    c = spearman(a,b) if method=='spearman' else pearson(a,b)
    return c, len(ts), T

results={}
for film, idents in ITEMS.items():
    rows=[]
    for ident in idents:
        try:
            for k in (2,3,5):
                c, n, T = item_corr(ident, k)
                rows.append((ident,k,c,n,T))
        except Exception as e:
            print(film, ident, 'ERR', e)
    if rows:
        # per item: take k=3 as headline; average across items
        k3 = [r[2] for r in rows if r[1]==3]
        k2 = [r[2] for r in rows if r[1]==2]
        k5 = [r[2] for r in rows if r[1]==5]
        results[film]={'k2':np.mean(k2),'k3':np.mean(k3),'k5':np.mean(k5),'peritem':[(r[0][:30],r[1],round(r[2],3)) for r in rows]}
        print(f"{film:10s} k2={np.mean(k2):+.3f} k3={np.mean(k3):+.3f} k5={np.mean(k5):+.3f}  (items: {len(k3)})")

json.dump(results, open('/tmp/results.json','w'), indent=1, default=float)
print()
order = sorted(results.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]['k3'])
print("RANK by k3:", [(f, round(v['k3'],3)) for f,v in order])
order = sorted(results.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]['k2'])
print("RANK by k2:", [(f, round(v['k2'],3)) for f,v in order])

from PIL import Image
import numpy as np, glob, re

def item_profile(pref):
    files = sorted(glob.glob(f'/tmp/thumbs/{pref}_*.jpg'))
    ts,lum=[],[]
    for f in files:
        ts.append(int(re.search(r'_(\d+)\.jpg', f).group(1)))
        a=np.asarray(Image.open(f).convert('RGB')).astype(float).mean(axis=2)
        rows=a.mean(axis=1); cols=a.mean(axis=0)
        rr=np.where(rows>12)[0]; cc=np.where(cols>12)[0]
        lum.append(a[rr[0]:rr[-1]+1, cc[0]:cc[-1]+1].mean() if len(rr) and len(cc) else a.mean())
    ts=np.array(ts,float); lum=np.array(lum)
    o=np.argsort(ts); ts,lum=ts[o],lum[o]
    k=np.ones(len(ts),bool); k[1:]=ts[1:]!=ts[:-1]
    return ts[k],lum[k]

mine=np.load('/tmp/profile.npy')
def smooth(y,k):
    ker=np.ones(2*k+1)/(2*k+1)
    return np.convolve(np.pad(y,k,mode='edge'),ker,mode='valid')
def ranknorm(y):
    r=np.argsort(np.argsort(y)); return r/(len(y)-1)
def spear(a,b):
    ra,rb=ranknorm(a),ranknorm(b)
    ra=ra-ra.mean(); rb=rb-rb.mean()
    return float((ra*rb).sum()/np.sqrt((ra*ra).sum()*(rb*rb).sum()))
